quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 conference call Q&A script summary (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 conference call Q&A summary, August 10, 2026; the company's FY2026 = year ending March 2027) on the Materials business: the profit forecast for Materials was raised because the planned switch of battery materials to new types was moved to FY2027 or later, reducing the expected volume decline and switching costs versus the earlier case of a switch in FY2026; advanced materials profits are also expected to rise on strong sales of Faraday rotators (a device material) and of applied powder materials supported by AI- and data-center-related demand.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 conference call Q&A script summary (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 conference call Q&A summary) on the outlook for Q2 onward: excluding the inventory-valuation effect in Smelting & Refining, profit slows after Q1 mainly because the forecast uses lower metal prices than Q1 actuals and the Middle East situation is expected to weigh more in the second half; the Materials segment expects costs for the switch to a new type of battery material in the second half, and the plan for higher Mineral Resources production in the second half than the first is unchanged. On the Middle East impact estimate, the breakdown has changed: in May about JPY 15.0 bn was assigned to Mineral Resources and about JPY 5.0 bn to Smelting & Refining, now updated to 50% each; by cost factor, energy-related items were about 80% in May and are now 50%, with the energy impact mainly higher diesel prices at overseas mines and the rest rising operating-material prices, especially externally procured sulfuric acid.
quarterly_data.figure: May estimate: Mineral Resources about JPY 15.0 bn, Smelting & Refining about JPY 5.0 bn; August: 50% each; energy share about 80% to 50%

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Metal Mining results briefing Q&A: FY2026 Q1 conference call Q&A script summary (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 conference call Q&A summary) on operations: the CBNC production plan was revised down because of equipment and ore-property issues the company finds difficult to make up; electrolytic copper production was lowered because equipment trouble in wet processing at the Toyo Smelter & Refinery in Q1 continues to force lower operating levels, expected to persist in Q2 and factored into the plan. Copper smelting TC/RC and electrolytic copper sales premiums have not changed significantly since the May forecast. The Quebrada Blanca copper mine is operating to plan and its tailings management facility measures are on plan, so management does not expect the TMF to affect 2026 operations as it did in 2025.
